title: Artin criterion over the integers with representable diagonal
statement: Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-size-convention]. A category fibred in groupoids means a category over schemes with cartesian lifts along every base map and groupoid fibres. Suppose: (i) isomorphisms between two objects form an etale sheaf and every etale descent datum for objects is effective; (ii) the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that the sheaf of isomorphisms of any two objects over a scheme is an algebraic space; (iii) for every small directed inverse system of affine schemes $T_i$ with limit $T$, the natural functor $\mathop{2\!\operatorname{colim}}_i\mathcal X(T_i)\to\mathcal X(T)$ is an equivalence, where the left side consists of objects at a stage and arrows at sufficiently late common stages; (iv) for every pushout $S'=S\amalg_TT'$ of spectra of Artinian local rings of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, with $T\to T'$ a thickening, the functor $\mathcal X(S')\to\mathcal X(S)\times_{\mathcal X(T)}\mathcal X(T')$ is an equivalence; (v) for every finite type field $K$ over $\mathbf Z$ and object $x_0\in\mathcal X(K)$, the tangent space (isomorphism classes of objects over $K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with identified special fibre $x_0$) and the infinitesimal automorphism space (automorphisms of the trivial such deformation inducing the identity on $x_0$) are finite-dimensional over $K$ [def-weil-field]; (vi) every compatible system $x_n\in\mathcal X(A/\mathfrak m^n)$ for a complete Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ with finite type residue field over $\mathbf Z$ is induced, with all transition isomorphisms, by an object over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; (vii) if a family over a scheme locally of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ is versal at a finite type point, it is versal at all finite type points of some open neighbourhood. Here a family $x$ over a scheme $U$ locally of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ is versal at a finite type point $u$ if the following lifting condition holds. For every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local rings with common residue field $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, a map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and a deformation over $A'$ of $x_u$ together with an isomorphism of its restriction with the pulled-back family over $A$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism with the given deformation extending that isomorphism. Assume also the usual size bound: the cardinalities of isomorphism classes and arrows in $\mathcal X(K)$ for finite type fields $K/\mathbf Z$ have a common bound by the size of a scheme in the chosen universe. Then $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack: it has the representable diagonal in (ii) and a smooth surjective atlas from a scheme, representable by algebraic spaces. Smoothness of morphisms representable by algebraic spaces is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A commutative local ring has a unique maximal ideal; it is Artinian when every descending chain of ideals stabilizes. A thickening here is a closed immersion defined by a nilpotent ideal. A finite type point $u$ of $U$ means that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The complete local systems in (vi) are indexed by integers $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 07Y4 (lemma-diagonal-representable), specialized to Spec Z; section-axioms [-1] through [3], definition-versal and definition-openness-versality. The specialization uses that Z and its localizations are G-rings.

proof.text: The integers are a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-z-g-ring]. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-smooth-point-neighbourhood] with $R=\mathbf Z$. Its five deformation assumptions are exactly (iii)--(vii), and its diagonal hypothesis is (ii). Thus for every finite type field $k/\mathbf Z$ and every isomorphism class $[x_0]$ in $\mathcal X(k)$, choose a finite type affine $U_{k,[x_0]}$, an object $x_{k,[x_0]}$, a point $u_{k,[x_0]}$ with residue field identified with $k$, and an isomorphism $x_{k,[x_0]}|_u\cong x_0$. The resulting map $h_{U_{k,[x_0]}}\to\mathcal X$ is smooth and representable by algebraic spaces.

Choose one representative of each finite type field over $\mathbf Z$ and each object isomorphism class in its fibre. These fields form a small set: each has a presentation as a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over $\mathbf Z$. The assumed common bound on the fibre cardinalities makes the resulting index set $I$ small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Form $U=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its inclusions are pairwise disjoint open immersions covering $U$. The objects $x_i$ have the unique descent identifications on the empty pairwise overlaps and the identity on self-overlaps; hypothesis (i) glues them to $x\in\mathcal X(U)$. For any scheme $V$ and $y\in\mathcal X(V)$, the sheaf of triples $(a:T\to U,b:T\to V,\alpha:a^*x\cong b^*y)$ is the pullback of the diagonal along $(x,y):U\times V\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$. Hypothesis (ii) therefore represents it by an algebraic space $W_V=U\times_{\mathcal X}V$. This proves representability of $h_U\to\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 07Y4, coproduct construction and its set-theoretical footnote.

proof.text: For the same $V,y$, the inverse images $W_i$ of the open-and-closed subschemes $U_i\subset U$ cover $W_V$. Each projection $W_i=U_i\times_{\mathcal X}V\to V$ is smooth by the defining test for the smooth morphism chosen in step 1. On a surjective etale scheme chart $P\to W_V$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], the inverse images $P_i$ cover $P$ by open subschemes. Each $P_i\to V$ is smooth, since it is an etale scheme chart of the smooth map $W_i\to V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source], $P\to V$ is smooth. Thus $W_V\to V$ is smooth by the chart definition, for every $V,y$, including an empty cover. Hence $h_U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 07Y4, assertion that the disjoint union map is smooth; chart-local verification written out.

proof.text: Now let $V$ be affine and locally of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $y\in\mathcal X(V)$. For every etale scheme chart $P\to W_V$, the smooth map $P\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Flatness and local finite presentation of algebraic-space morphisms are tested on these charts, so [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] applies to $W_V\to V$. Its image $O\subseteq|V|$ is open.

source.place: Tag 07Y4, paragraph beginning with the algebraic space W: smoothness makes its image open.

proof.text: The affine locally finitely presented scheme $V$ over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is of finite type: finite presentation gives finitely many algebra generators locally, and quasi-compactness of the affine source [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives a finite such affine cover [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $v\in V$ is a finite type point, then $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is of finite type by definition, and composition with $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Put $k=\kappa(v)$ and $x_0=y|_v$. The component indexed by $(k,[x_0])$ supplies $u$ and the specified isomorphism $x_i|_u\cong y|_v$. The triple $(u,v,\alpha)$ is a $k$-point of $W_V$ over $v$, so $v\in O$. This uses the isomorphism in the fibre product, not equality of the chosen object representatives. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-points-detect-open], the open $O$ containing every finite type point is all of $|V|$. Thus $W_V\to V$ is surjective for each such finite presentation affine test.

source.place: Tag 07Y4, final paragraph, using Morphisms Tag 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points).

proof.text: Hypothesis (iii), being an equivalence on the indicated $2$-colimits, implies in particular limit preservation on objects. The map $h_U\to\mathcal X$ is representable by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-limit-test-surjective-representable] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal F=h_U$, and $\mathcal G=\mathcal X$; step 5 gives exactly its tests on affine schemes locally of finite presentation. It follows that $W_V\to V$ is surjective for every scheme $V$ and every $y\in\mathcal X(V)$. Hence $h_U\to\mathcal X$ is a smooth surjective representable atlas.

source.place: Tag 07Y4, application of Criteria for Representability Tag 07WI (lemma-check-property-limit-preserving).

proof.text: Hypothesis (i) says that $\mathcal X$ is an etale stack, (ii) gives its representable diagonal, and steps 2--6 supply the smooth surjective scheme atlas. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]. It supplies fppf descent for objects and arrows, so $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack with this diagonal and this atlas, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 07Y4, invocation of Criteria for Representability Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale).
